aspects.fertilizer:
**Average Fertility Soil Nutrients:**
Apply fertilizers based on soil chemical analysis. One acre of average fertility soil requires 34 kilograms nitrogen, 23 kilograms phosphorus, and 12 kilograms potash. Alternative fertilizers can be used to supply these recommended quantities. Use balanced fertilizers to achieve top quality and protect against negative climate impacts.

**Irrigated Option 1:**
Apply 1 bag DAP and half bag SOP at sowing. Apply half bag urea with the first irrigation. Apply the remaining half bag urea with the second irrigation.

**Irrigated Option 2:**
Apply 2.5 bags of 18 percent SSP, half bag urea, and half bag MOP at sowing. Apply half bag urea with the first irrigation. Apply half bag urea with the second irrigation for the remaining nitrogen.

**Irrigated Option 3:**
Apply three-quarters bag nitrophos, 1.75 bags of 18 percent SSP, and half bag SOP or MOP at sowing. Apply 1 bag calcium ammonium nitrate with the first irrigation. Apply 1 bag calcium ammonium nitrate with the second irrigation.

**Rain-fed and Low Rainfall Areas:**
Rain-fed barani areas require three-fourths of the fertilizer dose used in irrigated areas. Low rainfall areas require half of the fertilizer dose. Apply the remaining nitrogen in two installments with rainfall.

**Quality and Micronutrients:**
Apply 2 kilograms sulfur per acre at sowing for best quality. Apply 2 kilograms sulfon or 2 kilograms sulphate of potash per acre at flowering.

**Crop Care and Climate Management:**
Thin the crop when it develops four leaves. Sow sesame on ridges in high rainfall areas or raw soils. Monitor weather forecasts to mitigate climate change effects. Drain excess water during heavy rains. Irrigate according to need during drought. Control weeds in the crop.

**Departmental Support:**
The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension formulates an integrated district strategy and mobilizes staff to achieve production targets. The Deputy Director of Agriculture assists with seed provision, and seed is also available from research institutes. The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension ensures companies maintain abundant stocks of fertilizers and agricultural pesticides for timely and easy availability to farmers.
aspects.harvesting:
Harvesting Time:
Sesame matures and is ready for harvest 100 to 120 days after sowing.
Harvest when the crop is fully ripe and the grain is hard.
Cut the crop when the lower 75 percent of pods turn yellowish and before the pods open.
Cut the crop using a sickle or a harvester.
Do not thresh the crop immediately after harvesting.

Field Handling and Drying:
Tie harvested plants into small bundles. 
Small bundles allow easy airflow and help immature pods ripen.
Stand bundles upright on a prepared, leveled, cleaned, and plastered floor.
Dust ash around the bundles to protect them from insects.
Dry the crop in open sunlight for 3 to 5 days to reduce moisture and dry the grain thoroughly.
Turn the crop over periodically during drying to ensure even drying and prevent fungus.

Threshing and Cleaning:
Shake pods when dry to separate the seed.
Repeat shaking 2 to 3 times at intervals to separate seeds completely.
Alternatively, feed the adequately dried crop into a thresher for threshing.
Dry the seeds in the sun for 2 to 3 days.
Clean the seeds when moisture reaches 8 to 10 percent.
Alternatively, clean threshed grain well and give it another 1 to 2 days of sun drying until moisture reaches about 10 to 12 percent.

Storage:
Store completely dry and clean grain in an airy and dry place to protect it from pests and diseases.
Use jute bags for storage.
Do not use plastic sacks.

Pesticide Safety:
Follow department instructions to control harmful pests and diseases.
Strictly observe the pre-harvest interval when applying agricultural poisons.
Never apply poisons after the pre-harvest interval to prevent toxic residues in the produce.
aspects.irrigation:
Ridge Sown Sesame Irrigation:
First irrigation is applied 15 to 20 days after complete germination. Second irrigation is applied at flowering. Third irrigation is applied when pods are fully formed. Ridge sowing generally requires 2 to 3 irrigations. Ensure water does not reach the top of the ridges during irrigation.

Flat Field Sesame Irrigation:
First irrigation is applied 40 to 45 days after sowing. Second irrigation is applied at flowering. Third irrigation is applied when pods are fully formed. Flat fields generally require 4 to 5 irrigations.

General Irrigation Practices:
Always apply light irrigation. Irrigate preferably in the morning or evening. Do not allow the crop to suffer from drought or water stress. Apply 1 to 2 additional irrigations as needed if the weather remains dry during pod formation. Irrigate as needed during drought or high temperatures.

Drainage and Rainy Areas:
Cultivate sesame on ridges in high rainfall areas or soft loose soils. Immediately drain excess water from the field during heavy rains to prevent standing water damage. Abnormal temperature variations and unseasonal rains increase pest and disease attacks. Monitor weather forecasts and follow departmental plant protection recommendations.

Disease Management:
Practice crop rotation to prevent root and stem rot. Do not cultivate sesame next year in fields affected by root and stem rot.

Thinning and Crop Care:
Thin the crop when it develops four leaves. Use balanced fertilizers. Apply 2 kg sulfur at sowing. Apply 2 kg sulfate of potash at flowering for best crop quality.

Weed Control:
For drill-sown sesame, mix pendimethalin 33 percent at 800 to 1000 ml per 120 liters of water and spray within 12 hours after sowing. Check weather forecasts before sowing and adjust the chemical dose if rain is expected. Rain may slightly affect the chemical initially, but plants recover. Perform one hoeing one month after applying weedicides. Alternatively, spray pendimethalin 33 percent at 1200 ml per acre before sowing with soaking irrigation and mix into the soil. Plow when workable moisture arrives, apply soaking irrigation again, and sow sesame at proper moisture level.
aspects.machinery:
Land Preparation:
Plow and plank two to three times to prepare the field thoroughly.
Level the land using a laser land leveler to maintain uniform field moisture and improve germination and growth.

Rain-fed Barani Areas:
After rainfall, prepare the field by plowing and planking two to three times when the soil reaches workable moisture condition.

Ridge Sowing:
NIAB Pearl, NIAB Till 2016, and NIAB Millennium are suitable varieties for ridge line sowing.
Keep row spacing at 2.5 feet because these varieties have wider plant spread.
Sow seeds at a depth not exceeding approximately 1 inch.
Make ridges using a tractor ridger when the crop height reaches approximately 6 inches, at an interval of 7 to 15 days, when the crop height is 1.5 to 2 feet.
Perform three to four hoeings.

High Rainfall Areas and Heavy Soils:
Broadcasting the crop protects it from excess water damage in heavy soils and high rainfall areas.
Broadcast the sesame seed and then make ridges using a ridger.
Maintain a distance of 3.5 feet between the ridges.
Tie a wooden beam behind the ridger like a plank to flatten the top surface of the ridges and cover seeds with a light layer of soil.
This method reduces the risk of rain damage and increases yield.
A ridger cum seeder machine is available for this method of sowing.
aspects.other:
**Weed Control:**
For drill sowing, spray Pendimethalin 33 percent at 800 to 1000 ml mixed in 120 liters of water per acre within 12 hours after sowing. Check the weather forecast before sowing and adjust the chemical dose if rain is expected. Rain can sometimes temporarily affect the chemical negatively, but plants recover and become healthy later. Perform one hoeing one month after applying weedicides. Alternatively, spray Pendimethalin 33 percent at 1200 ml per acre before sowing with rauni irrigation and incorporate it into the soil. Plow when workable soil moisture is reached, irrigate again, and sow sesame when workable moisture returns. Keep the crop free of weeds.

**Crop Management:**
Cultivate sesame on ridges in high-rainfall areas or soft soils. Thin the crop when plants reach the four-leaf stage. Use balanced fertilizers. Apply 2 kg of sulfur at sowing time and 2 kg of sulfate of potash at flowering time to obtain the best quality.

**Climate and Weather Management:**
Unusual temperature fluctuations and untimely rains cause damage and increase pest and disease attacks. Stay informed through meteorological department forecasts. Provide special crop care and follow departmental plant protection recommendations. Drain excess water during surplus rains. Irrigate as needed during drought or high temperatures.

**Agricultural Extension and Administration:**
The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension formulates an integrated strategy to increase sesame production in the district. The Deputy Director informs the provincial government and mobilizes staff to achieve assigned targets. Extension staff provides training to farmers at the tehsil and markaz levels suited to local conditions and the sesame crop. Staff continuously assesses on-site agricultural problems during the season, finds suitable solutions through agricultural workers, and conveys them to farmers.
aspects.overview:
Overview and Uses:
Sesame is an ancient oilseed crop cultivated primarily for edible oil.
Seeds contain over 50 percent edible oil and over 22 percent good quality protein.
Its oil properties closely resemble olive oil.
Seeds are used in food, sweets, bakery products, and fast food.
The oil is used in pharmaceuticals, high-quality soaps, perfumes, and carbon paper.
Blending 5 to 10 percent sesame oil into other edible oil increases its utility.
Sesame oil cake is feed for livestock and poultry.
The crop is exported to earn foreign exchange.

Punjab Statistics:
In 2020-21, cultivated area was 367.84 thousand acres (148.86 thousand hectares), production was 90.66 thousand tonnes, and average yield was 608.83 kilograms per hectare (6.16 maunds per acre).
In 2021-22, cultivated area was 437.00 thousand acres (176.85 thousand hectares), production was 115.8 thousand tonnes, and average yield was 654.81 kilograms per hectare (6.62 maunds per acre).
In 2022-23, cultivated area was 607.12 thousand acres (245.70 thousand hectares), production was 148.22 thousand tonnes, and average yield was 603.26 kilograms per hectare (6.10 maunds per acre).
In 2023-24, cultivated area was 929.94 thousand acres (376.32 thousand hectares), production was 287.37 thousand tonnes, and average yield was 764.00 kilograms per hectare (7.73 maunds per acre).
In 2024-25, cultivated area was 1761.95 thousand acres (713.00 thousand hectares), production was 420.88 thousand tonnes, and average yield was 590.00 kilograms per hectare (5.97 maunds per acre).

Varieties:
TH-6 is a single-branched variety that flowers in 30 to 35 days, sets pods up to the top, and matures in about 110 days.
TS-5 is a branched, disease-resistant variety that flowers in 40 to 45 days and matures in about 125 days.
Black King is a branched, high-yielding, black-seeded, disease-resistant variety suitable for pharmaceuticals that matures in 110 to 115 days.
NIAB Til-2016 was released in 2016.
NIAB Til-2016 is branched, disease-resistant, resists lodging with a strong stem, has shiny white plants and seeds, bears 200 to 300 capsules per plant, and matures in 95 to 100 days.
NIAB Til-2016 sowing time is April 15 to August 10, spacing is 2.5 feet by 9 to 12 inches, and seed rate is 1 kilogram.

Soil Requirements:
Medium to heavy loam soil with good water absorption and moisture retention capacity is suitable.
Clayey, non-absorbing soils are unsuitable.
Excessively sandy, waterlogged, saline, and low-lying soils are unsuitable.

Government and Extension Support:
The provincial government sets district acreage targets with federal government approval and publishes sesame production plans.
Agriculture Extension and Pest Warning field staff inspect fields and notify farmers when pests exceed economic threshold levels.
Farmer and staff training on modern technology is conducted at district, tehsil, and markaz levels.
The Directorate of Agricultural Information runs print and electronic media awareness campaigns from sowing to harvest.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Management:
Drain excess rainwater and irrigate during dry heat. Do not hoe immediately after spraying to prevent chemical breakdown, weed regrowth, and inhaling toxic dust. Observe pre-harvest intervals on pesticide labels.

Variety TH-6:
This variety faces higher attack from jassid and mirid bug.

Root and Stem Rot:
Caused by Macrophomina phaseolina, producing brown roots and black stem spots. Rotate crops, avoid planting sesame in affected fields next year, prevent drought, and keep irrigation below ridge tops.

Wilt:
Fusarium oxysporum rots roots and wilts plants completely without reviving after watering. Rotate crops and avoid drought.

Collar Rot:
Phytophthora megasperma spreads via irrigation water, forming an enlarging black ring around stems. Uproot diseased plants. Plant on ridges so water avoids stems. Plow empty fields in May. Spray lower stems with 250 grams per acre Metalaxyl plus Mancozeb or Fosetyl-aluminium in water.

Stem Blight:
Spreads in hot humid conditions and July to August rains, turning stems black and brittle with brown spots. Spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 milliliters Difenoconazole plus Azoxystrobin per liter of water.

Sesame Phyllody:
Phytoplasma spread by sucking insects turns flowers into sterile leafy structures. Control sucking insects, destroy infected plants, and avoid sowing early.

Leaf Roller:
Larvae web leaves and bore into pods. Economic threshold is 8 to 10 percent plant damage. Spray per acre 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC, 200 milliliters Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, 50 milliliters Chlorantraniliprole 20 SC, 200 milliliters Lufenuron 50 EC, or 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC.

Whitefly:
Economic threshold is 5 adults or nymphs per leaf. Spray per acre 200 grams Pyriproxyfen WG, 125 milliliters Spirotetramat 240 SC mixed with 250 milliliters Bio powder, 80 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 500 milliliters Pyriproxyfen 10.8 EC.

Jassid:
Economic threshold is 1 adult or nymph per leaf. Spray per acre 100 grams Diafenthiuron 20 SG, 200 milliliters Nitenpyram 10 AS, 400 milliliters Dimethoate 40 EC, 250 milliliters Acephate 75 SP, or 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 WG.

Mirid Bug:
Attacks during flowering and pod formation. Economic threshold is over 6 per plant. Spray per acre 400 milliliters Dimethoate 40 EC, 100 milliliters Imidacloprid 200 SL, 100 milliliters Nitenpyram 10 AS, or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cotton Mealybug:
Spray twigs immediately upon appearance. Apply per 100 liters water 500 milliliters Malathion 57 EC, 800 milliliters Profenofos 500 EC, 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC, or 250 milliliters Imidacloprid 200 SL.

Thrips:
Economic threshold is 5 adults or nymphs per leaf. Spray per acre 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 200 milliliters Tolstenpyram 10 AS, 80 milliliters Chlorfenapyr 360 SC, 300 milliliters Emamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, or 250 grams Acephate 75 SP.

Rain-fed and Thar Areas:
Termites attack underground stems and roots in dry conditions. Economic threshold is 5 percent damage. Flood per acre with irrigation 1.5 to 2 liters Chlorpyrifos 40 EC or 1 to 1.5 liters Fipronil SC.

Harvesting and Storage:
Harvest when lower 75 percent pods turn yellow, before opening. Bundle upright, shake 2 to 3 times when dry, and sun-dry seed to 8 to 10 percent moisture before storage.
aspects.sowing:
General Sowing:
General sesame sowing time is June 1 to July 15.
Medium to heavy loam soil with good water absorption and moisture retention is suitable.
Prepare land by ploughing and planking 2 to 3 times.
Level land with a laser land leveler to maintain uniform moisture.
Sow in tar wattar conditions.
Do not sow in low wattar or excess wattar.
Sow in the morning or evening when heat intensity is low.
Seed depth must not exceed approximately 1 inch.
Sow according to weather forecasts so rain does not occur before emergence.

Southern Punjab:
May is suitable for sowing in hot and dry areas.
NIAB Faisalabad varieties can also be sown in June and July.

Barani Areas:
Sow in April and May after rain in tar wattar.
Prepare land by ploughing and planking 2 to 3 times when wattar arrives after rain.

Variety Specifications:
TS-3 was released in 2000, sows April 15 to May 30, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2 to 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches.
TS-5 was released in 2011, sows May 1 to June 15, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2 to 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches.
TS-6 or TH-6 was released in 2009, sows May 1 to May 30, requires 2 kg seed per acre, row spacing 1.5 feet, and plant spacing 6 inches.
Anmol Til was released in 2023, sows May 1 to May 30, requires 2 kg seed per acre, row spacing 1.5 feet, and plant spacing 6 inches.
Black King was released in 2021, sows May 15 to June 15, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2 to 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches.
NIAB Pearl was released in 2017, sows April 15 to July 31, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches or 10 to 12 inches.
NIAB Til-2016 was released in 2016, sows April 15 to August 10, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches or 10 to 12 inches.
NIAB Magneem or NIAB Millennium was released in 2022, sows June 15 to July 31, requires 1 kg seed per acre, row spacing 2.5 feet, and plant spacing 9 to 12 inches or 10 to 12 inches.
NIAB Faisalabad varieties can also be sown in March depending on weather.

Drill Sowing:
Sow using a single row drill or small seed drill.
Keep the pore opening minimal.
Mix 1 acre of seed with 6 to 8 kg of sand or fine soil before placing it into the seed box.
Stir the seed with a stick during sowing to prevent choking.

Broadcasting:
If a drill is unavailable, mix 1 acre of seed with 2 to 3 kg of sand or fine soil.
Perform a double broadcast by scattering seed once lengthwise and then crosswise.
Mix seed into soil using light ploughing and planking.

Heavy Soils and High Rainfall Areas:
Broadcast seed and make ridges 3.5 feet apart using a tractor ridger.
Tie a wooden log behind the ridger to level ridge tops and cover seed with light soil.
A ridger-cum-seeder machine can also be used.

Ridge Planting and Cultivation:
NIAB Pearl, NIAB Til-2016, and NIAB Millennium are suitable for ridges at 2.5 feet row spacing due to wide plant spread.
When plants reach 6 inches height, form ridges with a tractor ridger at 7 to 15 days intervals until plants reach 1.5 to 2 feet height.
Perform 3 to 4 hoeings.
Thin plants to recommended spacing when the crop reaches 4 leaves.
Perform one dry hoeing before the first irrigation.
Perform a second hoeing after irrigation when wattar arrives.
aspects.varieties:
**Regions and Timing:**
NIAB Faisalabad varieties can be sown in March.
In barani areas, sow in April and May after rain in wet moisture.
In hot, dry Southern Punjab, sow in May, or sow NIAB Faisalabad varieties in June or July.
Sow sesame only when rain is not forecasted until after emergence.

**Soil and Sowing Method:**
Medium to heavy loam soil with water absorption and moisture retention is suitable.
Sow in wet moisture morning or evening using a single-row or small seed drill.
Never sow in excessive or low moisture.
Keep seed depth under one inch.
Mix one acre of seed with 6 to 8 kilograms of sand or fine soil, use minimal drill hole opening, and stir seed during drilling.

**Ridge Cultivation:**
NIAB Pearl, NIAB Til-2016, and NIAB Millennium suit ridge planting.
Keep 2.5 feet between rows and 10 to 12 inches between plants.
When crop is 6 inches tall, wait 7 to 15 days until 1.5 to 2 feet tall, make ridges with a tractor ridger, and do 3 to 4 hoeings.

**Single-Branched Varieties:**
These varieties have early flowering and disease resistance.
Both require 2 kilograms seed per acre, 1.5 feet row spacing, and 6 inches plant spacing.
Anmol Til was released in 2023, is sown May 1 to May 30, forms clustered pods, and yields around 25 maunds per acre.
TH-6 was released in 2009, is sown May 1 to May 30, flowers in 30 to 35 days, pods reach the top, and matures in 110 days.
TH-6 suffers heavy green jassid and mirid bug attacks.

**Branched Varieties:**
These disease-resistant varieties require 1 kilogram seed per acre, 2 to 2.5 feet row spacing, and 9 to 12 inches plant spacing.
TS-3 was released in 2000, is sown April 15 to May 30, tolerates climate fluctuations, and matures in 90 to 100 days.
TS-5 was released in 2011, is sown May 1 to June 15, flowers in 40 to 45 days, and matures in 125 days.
Black King was released in 2021, is sown May 15 to June 15, has black seeds, matures in 110 to 115 days, and suits medicine production.
NIAB Til-2016 was released in 2016, is sown April 15 to August 10, resists lodging, matures in 95 to 100 days, has shiny white plants and seeds, and bears 200 to 300 capsules per plant.
NIAB Pearl was released in 2017, is sown April 15 to July 31, has dark green leaves, resists lodging, matures in 100 to 115 days, and bears 7 to 14 branches and 200 to 300 capsules per plant.
NIAB Millennium was released in 2022, is sown June 15 to July 31, has close pod spacing on strong stems, matures in 100 to 105 days, and bears 300 to 400 capsules per plant.

**Departmental Support:**
Deputy Director Agriculture Extension and research institutes provide seed.
The department ensures fertilizer and pesticide stocks, training staff and farmers at district and tehsil levels.
Apply departmental-recommended chemicals at label doses, observing pre-harvest intervals.
aspects.weeds:
Thinning and Hoeing:
Thin sesame when the crop develops four leaves.
Maintain the recommended plant-to-plant distance during thinning.
Perform one dry hoeing before the first irrigation.
Perform the second hoeing after irrigation when workable moisture arrives.
Perform one hoeing one month after applying weedicides.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after spraying weedicide.
Immediate hoeing breaks the chemical effect and allows weeds to regrow.
Immediate hoeing also raises chemical dust into the air, which can enter the farmer's body and breath, causing severe health harm.

Chemical Weed Control:
In drill sowing, mix 800 to 1000 ml of Pendimethalin 33 percent in 120 liters of water.
Spray this mixture within 12 hours after sowing.
Always check the weather forecast before sowing.
If rain is expected, set the chemical quantity carefully.
Rain sometimes has a slight adverse effect on the chemical, but plants recover and become healthy later.
In the second method, spray 1200 ml of Pendimethalin 33 percent per acre before sowing with pre-soaking irrigation and mix it into the soil.
Plow the field when workable moisture arrives, apply pre-soaking irrigation again, and sow sesame when workable moisture returns.

High Rainfall and Soft Soils:
Sow sesame on ridges in high rainfall areas or on soft soils.
Drain excess water from the field during excessive rains.
Provide irrigation as needed during drought conditions.
Stay informed through meteorological weather forecasts to reduce the impacts of climate change.

Fertilizer and Crop Care:
Control weeds in the sesame crop.
Apply balanced fertilizers.
Apply 2 kg of sulfur at the time of sowing.
Apply 2 kg of sulfate of potash at the flowering stage to achieve the best crop quality.
